title: Console minimal surface — rollback matrix and acceptance gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Trim the initial Console Insights surface so we can launch a stable, low-cost MVP while preserving the minimum operational and debug workflows for production teams. This ticket captures the decision matrix for which features will be cut vs. deferred, the rollback / fallback modes we will ship, and the acceptance gates that must be satisfied before launch.

Background: During alpha testing and early telemetry, the full Insights card set and live trace integration pushed engineering effort and runtime cost beyond our Phase 1 budget. Product teams have agreed to a surgical minimal surface that preserves: per-route latency histograms, route-level token cost breakdown, and a compact trace snapshot for error investigation. Non-essential features such as ad-hoc trace exploration, per-user cost attribution, and custom card composition are deferred to subsequent phases.

Decision matrix (summary):
- Keep in MVP: route-level latency p50/p95, total token spend per route (24h rolling), card for recent errors with trace id linking, model-version selector default.
- Defer: long-retention analytics (>30d), full span flamegraphs, per-user cost breakdown, interactive trace explorer, custom dashboard creation.
- Rollback modes: when backend cannot support sampling rates, Console will show an explanatory degraded mode and a single-point fallback metric (95th latency only) and link to the consolidated logs in Datadog. For cost breakdown unavailability, show cached 24h snapshot and a missing-data flag with remediation steps.

Why this cut: Reduces initial query load by ~45%, lowers storage needs for traces by ~70% (sampling + compact capture), and removes several heavy UI surfaces that require continued investment in instrumentation and backend indices. This aligns with the production-first thesis: smallest surface that yields operational value (incident triage + cost visibility) with SLA-friendly budget.

Acceptance criteria (must all be satisfied for Done):
1) Backend: route latency and token cost endpoints return within 200ms P95 for 95% of requests under expected load profile (verified in load test harness).
2) Traces: compact trace snapshot captures top-level spans + error context and can be retrieved within 500ms in 95th percentile; sampling config defaults to 1% and is plumbed through the runtime.
3) UI: Minimal Insight card set (3 cards per route) renders on first paint within 800ms on a 3G-equivalent synthetic test.
4) Degraded UX: When sampling or cost pipeline is unavailable, the Console shows clear degraded-mode messaging, a cached snapshot where available, and a single-click link to logs/alerts.
5) Documentation: PRD updated with cut list and rollback matrix; runway playbook for on-call with steps to flip sampling and reenable features.
6) Telemetry: New metric flags implemented to track percentage of requests returned in degraded mode and overall cost delta vs baseline.
7) Stakeholder signoff: PM, Design, and Eng leads have reviewed and approved the cut list and rollback behaviors.
Acceptance_criteria_list: Backend latency endpoints P95 <=200ms under load
UI first paint <=800ms for minimal cards on 3G synthetic
Degraded-mode messaging and cached snapshot present when pipeline unavailable
PRD and runbook updated and linked
Telemetry flags added to track degraded-mode percentage
out_of_scope: Interactive trace explorer, long-term retention analytics (>30 days), per-user billing attribution, custom dashboard composer, RBAC feature gates for alpha MVP.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Teams may need per-user billing earlier than planned. Mitigation: Provide sample export to CSV and quick-runbook for finance teams; surface an early signal via the cost-alerting beta.
Risk: Reduced trace sampling may miss intermittent errors. Mitigation: Provide an on-demand higher-sampling toggle for canary routes and documented steps for temporarily raising sample rate during incidents.

release_notes_blurb: Console: Minimal Insights launch — initial set of route-level metrics, compact trace snapshots for quick triage, and cost-overview cards. Some advanced analytics deferred; degraded-mode UX will surface when backends are unavailable.
